report.tagline: A UK online-only supermarket that runs on robot warehouses, and a technology company that sells those robots to grocers around the world.
report.simpleSummary: Ocado is two businesses. First, Ocado.com is a UK online supermarket with no shops: you order a weekly shop and a van brings it in a one-hour slot. It sells M&S food and big brands. Second, Ocado builds giant warehouses where thousands of robots pick groceries, and licenses that system to supermarkets like Kroger in the US and Coles in Australia.

overview.whatItDoes: Ocado Retail sells groceries online in the UK and delivers them from large automated warehouses called customer fulfilment centres. Ocado Group's Technology Solutions arm designs the robots, software and vans and licenses them to grocers worldwide for upfront and ongoing fees.
howItWorks: Customers order on Ocado.com or the app, usually a full weekly shop, and choose a one-hour delivery slot.
In a customer fulfilment centre (CFC), thousands of robots move on a grid above stacked crates, bringing items to pickers or robot arms.
An average order of about 50 items can be picked in minutes, with very high accuracy and little waste.
Vans leave on routes planned by software and deliver in the chosen slot, with live tracking.
Partners like Kroger, Coles, Aeon and Lotte pay Ocado fees to build and run CFCs with its tech.
Ocado Zoom offered rapid delivery in parts of London, but Ocado's core is planned weekly shops, not 10-minute delivery.
overview.valueProposition: For shoppers: a full weekly shop with M&S food and big brands, delivered accurately in a one-hour slot. For grocers: a ready-made online system that is cheaper per order than store picking at scale.

businessModel.summary: Ocado Retail earns money by selling groceries online at a margin. Ocado Group earns fees from licensing its warehouse technology to grocers worldwide. The tech business costs a lot upfront, and its success depends on partners getting enough online orders.

revenueStreams.detail: UK grocery sales, shared 50/50 with M&S.
Upfront fees and ongoing fees from partners using CFCs.
Brands pay for ads on Ocado.com.
Payments such as Kroger's after closing CFCs, which inflated H1 2026 revenue.

businessModel.pricing: Delivery fees vary by slot and order size; free delivery on larger orders at off-peak slots. Smart Pass is a monthly membership. Partner fees are not public.
costDrivers: Building and running CFCs, including robots and buildings
Research and development for robots and software
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £120 weekly shop, Ocado Retail might earn about £30 in gross margin. Picking in a robot warehouse might cost a few pounds, and delivery about £8 to £10. Marketing and overheads take a few more pounds. At high volume, this can be profitable; at low volume, the fixed cost of the CFC makes each order lose money. That is the problem Kroger faced, leading it to close some CFCs.

howTheyGetUsers: Price matching with Tesco on some items
growth.moat: Ocado has over 20 years of building robot warehouses and software, with many patents. Few companies can match its system. But the moat is only valuable if grocers have enough online orders to fill the warehouses.

pmLessons: Great technology needs enough demand. Kroger's CFC closures show the cost of overestimating demand.
Fixed costs change unit economics. More orders make each one cheaper.
Owning a full system is a strong moat, but partners need to succeed for it to matter.
Planned weekly shops and 10-minute top-ups solve different problems; pick the job your product does best.

interviewQuestions.question: Kroger closed some Ocado CFCs. What went wrong, and what would you change?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain that online demand in those regions was lower than planned, so a huge fixed-cost warehouse sat half empty. Suggest smaller sites, phased builds or help for partners to grow demand, and track orders per week per CFC.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Ocado with Blinkit in India.
interviewQuestions.hint: Ocado does planned 50-item weekly shops from giant robot warehouses; Blinkit does 10-minute, 5-item top-ups from small dark stores. Compare cost per order, basket size and which customer job each one does best.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Ocado Retail's customer base?
interviewQuestions.hint: The main barrier is the belief that Ocado is expensive. Ideas: price match badges, M&S exclusives, first-shop offers. Measure new customers and 90-day retention, with gross margin as a guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Ocado's north star metric, and how would you break it down?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly orders delivered complete and on time. Split it into active customers, order frequency, order quality and warehouse utilisation, each with two or three inputs a team can move.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Ocado relaunch a rapid delivery service like Zoom?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh demand for top-ups against the cost of small sites that do not use Ocado's robots. Suggest a time-boxed test in one dense London area with clear stop rules.
